notes:
Strategy: scripted generator-based state machine with damped-least-squares IK (multi-seed global IK for reachability + per-step Cartesian servo with nullspace pull toward the global solution for straight-line motions). Top-down palm-down grasp aligned to the cube's faces (choosing the most reachable of the 4 yaw candidates), slow closure ramp, lift, verify the cube is held. Placement: cube 1 is dropped in the far half of the bin (along +x for the left bin, along +y for the right bin because of arm reach), then cube 2 (still held, bottom just below rim) is used to push cube 1 flush against the far wall; the hand then backs off so cube 2 clears cube 1 and releases cube 2 into the remaining 6 cm slot. Closed-loop corrections use observed cube position and yaw before release (hand yaw adjusted so the cube is axis-aligned with the bin). If cube 2 ends up raised (on cube 1 / wall), it retries by re-grasping and re-dropping while time remains.
Known weaknesses: ~65-75% success on practice seeds. The main failure is cube 2 landing tilted on cube 1 or the wall edge after a ~3 cm drop (the hand cannot enter the bin for an off-center set-down), especially for the right bin where the arm's reach is marginal (IK stalls, push less effective). Re-grasping a tilted cube inside the bin is unreliable. Sensing bias in cube position/yaw directly affects the tight (1 cm slack) fit.
